tldr: Canadian competitors are pushing on investing breadth and switching incentives. CIBC is adding Canadian Depositary Receipts (CDRs), including one on Anthropic after its U.S. IPO, while Wealthsimple tests a CAD stablecoin and a promotional-rate product. Elsewhere, OpenAI's ChatGPT Wallet and Kalshi's stock perpetuals point to agentic payments and trading outside regular hours.
themes: Expanding retail investing access (CDRs, ETFs, fractional global exposure)

highlights.headline: CIBC will launch a CDR on Anthropic following its U.S. IPO and is adding another CDR, taking its lineup to 145 across six countries.
highlights.why: A direct competitor is making access to hot U.S. names a differentiator, and it sets a bar for how quickly Simplii can offer comparable exposure to its self-directed investors.

highlights.headline: Wealthsimple opened a retail beta for Tetra's Canadian-dollar stablecoin and a CADD beta with 3.25% promotional rewards.
highlights.why: Wealthsimple is testing CAD-denominated digital money and promotional yield at the same time, which could reset customer expectations for cash products and moving money.

highlights.headline: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Wallet, letting AI agents pay for purchases without seeing card details.
highlights.why: Agent-initiated payments could change how customers pay and which accounts and cards sit behind the wallet, so the team should consider how Simplii products would work in that flow.

highlights.headline: Kalshi's U.S.-regulated stock perpetuals passed $1.75B traded in their first week, with about 39% of volume outside regular weekday hours. Kalshi has also bought a securities firm to move into stock trading.
highlights.why: Strong off-hours demand shows appetite for night, Sunday and leveraged trading, a category shift that puts pressure on traditional brokerage hours.
